rationale: PART_OF, TAKEN AT R3 (no grammar change: `preproc_include` is a NAMED node type of the served build). The contract's test (src/ast/types.ts:148-160) is that a part shares the library's single scope, imports nothing, and cannot be resolved as a separate module — which is a QUOTED include, and is NOT an angle include (that names another module's header and stays `imports`). MEASURED over the admitted population before the emission: 51,874 include sites = 39,665 QUOTED + 12,209 angle-bracket (script/m14/cpp-four-types-census.ts, validation/m14/measurements/cpp-four-types-census.json). THE DIRECTION IS THE DIRECTIVE'S OWN: source = the including unit (file scope), target = the part. THE TARGET IS A PATH, NOT THE SPECIFIER, because a specifier is a path and no resolver can bind it (the fsharp lane's measured rule on the same construct) — the target is the including file's directory joined with the specifier. metadata.partRole is MANDATORY and is "part" for a part_of_directive, which is the only written form C++ has. THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF: the edge exists only when the directive reaches the analyzer as a REAL preproc_include node, so a recovery-text regression drops BOTH rows and fails both ways. FALSIFIER OF THE EMISSION: an include site whose target resolves to a separate module in the same project — that would retire `part_of` for that site and put it back on `imports`.

expectRelationships.note: THE TARGET IS NOW PINNED, BECAUSE IT IS NOW STABLE. It was left unconstrained while it was a PATH - a path varies with the checkout, and pinning one would have made the fixture a test of the machine. It is now the part's MODULE SYMBOL (its file stem), the same on every machine and the only form the arbiter can bind: MEASURED path => 0 resolved of 4,612 and symbol => 383 resolved of 4,612, same population, same 2,000-file stride sample, the target's FORM the only variable. A CONSTRAINT THAT CAN NOW BE PINNED IS A CHECK THAT SHOULD NOW BE OWNED, so this fixture asserts the stem itself rather than merely that some part_of row exists.
